title:
Understand.
Try it.

description: From your first wallet to your own node — a practical guide to People’s Blockchain.
noticeText: Mainnet has not launched. Available operations depend on the site connection and network version. Test coins are not a promise of income.

cards.title: I’m getting started
cards.text: A wallet, PPL and your first transfer

sections.title: How People works
sections.lead: A blockchain is a shared record of operations. Your wallet signs an action, nodes verify it, and validators include it in blocks.

items.title: PPL is the network coin
items.text: People (PPL) pays for network fees and protocol operations. Test PPL is for testing the network; holding it does not mean you have earned money.

items.title: Participant, node, validator
items.text: A participant uses wallets and applications. A full node stores and verifies network state. A validator also produces and attests to blocks. A phone or an open browser tab does not automatically become a validator.

items.title: How the network is assembled
items.text: Each node keeps the chain state on its own disk. Validators produce and attest to blocks; ordinary follower nodes verify everything and produce nothing. The wallet, explorer, swap and factories on this site all read that same chain — see /explorer for the live state. Fee shares, supply rules and accounting live in the protocol code, so a page on this website cannot change them.

items.title: Where every fee goes
items.text: Every protocol fee is split by fixed shares: 30% to validators, 25% to the Community Pool, 20% to the treasury, 10% to liquidity and 15% to Growth, with 0% burned — fractional fees included. Protocol v2 applies the same shares to fractional fees, calculated in the smallest PPL units with the remainder going to validators. Contract gas is prepaid and unused gas is not refunded.

items.title: Buybacks
items.text: 100% of token and NFT launch fees (USDC/USDT) go to public PPL buybacks — including test stablecoin (tUSDC/tUSDT) fees through the StableFeeGateway. 30% of network fees go to public PPL buybacks (treasury 20% + liquidity 10%). The remaining 70% of network fees go to validators (30%), the community pool (25%) and the Growth Pool (15%). It all ultimately goes back to participants. Buybacks run on a published cadence through the 2-of-3 treasury multisig, and every purchase is visible in the explorer. Bought-back PPL is then split 30/25/20/10/15. Figures are preliminary and subject to community governance.

items.title: Running a node
items.text: Anyone can run a follower node with one Docker command: it verifies blocks and needs no wallet, bond or private keys. A validator is a separate role: it needs its own key, a bond and coordination with the operator, produces blocks, and must stay online. A phone or an open browser tab takes part in the network but is not a validator.

items.title: From signature to confirmation
items.text: An operation passes checks and enters a queue. Queue acceptance is not block inclusion or finality. Check the outcome in the explorer.

sections.title: Start with a wallet
sections.lead: You do not need your own server to get started.

items.title: 01 · Create or restore a wallet
items.text: Open the wallet and create a new one or restore your own. Keep the recovery phrase somewhere safe outside the website. A password protects local storage; it does not replace a backup of your phrase.

items.title: 02 · Check the connection
items.text: The wallet should show Testnet status. If the network seems unavailable, wait a moment and refresh the page.

items.title: 03 · Get test PPL
items.text: If the faucet is enabled on this network, request test coins through the available interface. Limits apply. Do not buy test coins on the promise of future income.

items.title: 04 · Try a small transfer
items.text: Check the recipient, amount and fee. Leave some PPL for later operations. After sending, find the transaction ID in the explorer and check block inclusion.

sections.title: Ways to take part
sections.lead: The network is in its test stage. These are participation mechanisms, not a promise of profit.

items.title: Validation · test protocol
items.text: Rewards depend on validator participation and network parameters. Registration, a bond and running infrastructure are required. Account for server costs and protocol risks; there is no promised fixed yield. Running an ordinary non-validator node does not earn a reward by itself.

items.title: Building products · depends on demand
items.text: You can test tokens, NFTs and contracts. Creating an asset does not create buyers, liquidity or profit. The protocol cannot guarantee product value or demand.

items.title: Growth referrals
items.text: Two levels, L1 and L2. The 70/30 weights apply to an eligible settlement budget, not the amount of every transfer. Activity, participation age, maturation and caps apply. An invitation alone does not earn a payment. View and claim Growth rewards through the partner portal when you qualify.

items.title: Mobile participation
items.text: One-tap participation sessions from your phone. Rewards depend on verified activity, not on keeping a page open or mining PPL.

items.title: Proof of humanity
items.text: Multi-signal checks without biometrics or raw personal data stored on-chain.

items.title: Participation points
items.text: Points set your share of Community Pool rewards from network fees. They cannot be bought or transferred.

sections.title: Build on the test network
sections.lead: Choose a tool and verify the result in the explorer.

items.title: Token
items.text: Choose issuance parameters and understand the allocation rules. The built-in token issuance mechanism allocates 10% of a new token to its community pool. This is not an automatic payment to every PPL holder or a universal rule for arbitrary Solidity contracts.

items.title: NFT
items.text: Prepare metadata and an image, check your rights to the materials and review the fee. An available form does not mean minting is complete: a signed operation must be included in a block.

items.title: Contract
items.text: Deployment requires PPL for gas and source review. Successful compilation is not a security audit. Test operations without real value first.

sections.title: Where fees go
sections.lead: A fee pays for a network operation; the transfer amount and its fee are different amounts.

items.title: distribution
items.text: The approved shares of applicable PPL fees are validators 30%, Community Pool 25%, Treasury 20%, Liquidity / Ecosystem 10%, Growth Pool 15%, burn 0%. These are shares, not a user yield.

items.title: Fractional fees
items.text: Protocol v2 applies the same shares to fractional fees, calculated in the smallest PPL units with the remainder going to validators. With no validators, their share goes to Treasury. The operator must coordinate a network-wide transition before applying the upgrade.

items.title: Check before signing
items.text: Different operations have different prices. Contract gas is prepaid; the current mechanism does not refund unused gas on success or revert. The fees page lists the values used by the website.

sections.title: Connect your own node
sections.lead: The new joining path uses a ready-made Docker image and one command. No private repository access, wallet or private keys are required.

items.title: 01 · Prepare Docker
items.text: Install Docker and make sure it is running. The first verified image targets Linux amd64 (x86-64). Other platforms are not yet advertised as verified.

items.title: 02 · Wait for the public release
items.text: Use the command in the panel above. It is pinned to the current public testnet release. Do not substitute other images or network URLs.

items.title: 03 · Copy and run the command
items.text: The command downloads a pinned image version, creates the people-node container and the persistent people-node-data volume. Network settings are fetched automatically over HTTPS and saved in the volume. Ordinary followers do not need to choose keys or edit an .env file.

items.title: 04 · Wait for synchronization
items.text: Your node connects to the archive seed, receives blocks from genesis and verifies signatures and state changes itself. Time depends on history length and your connection. The API is available only on your computer; ordinary joining does not require opening inbound ports.

items.title: 05 · Verify the result
items.text: Open http://localhost:4001/health and http://localhost:4001/chain/head. API availability alone does not prove synchronization: compare height and block data with the network. The next section covers verification and maintenance commands.

sections.title: Verify and maintain your node
sections.lead: Check synchronization, then manage the existing container. Do not repeat docker run each time you want to start your node.

items.title: Check the state
items.text: After startup, run the commands below on your computer. /health should return JSON with ok:true. /chain/head shows your local height — compare it with the public explorer. A successful /health alone does not prove full sync. The local API has no login; ignore unrelated 401 errors on other websites.

items.title: Logs, stop and restart
items.text: docker logs --tail 100 people-node shows recent messages. docker stop people-node shuts it down gracefully; docker start people-node starts the same container with its saved chain. Restart uses pinned settings even if the configuration server is temporarily unavailable.

items.title: Keep your data
items.text: Keep the people-node-data volume: it contains the chain and pinned network configuration. For manual startup, preserve DATA_DIR. Do not run docker compose down -v for data you need. The /snapshot response is a state overview, not a backup. Use a separate volume for another network.

items.title: Joining an older chain
items.text: Nodes retain a limited history window. An empty node may not catch up if early blocks have already been removed. The new v2 network has an archive mode: a dedicated node retains blocks from genesis for full verification. Enabling archive mode cannot recover previously deleted blocks.

sections.title: For developers: manual build
sections.lead: An optional path for developers with source access. Ordinary Docker users do not need this section.

items.title: 01 · Get the approved version
items.text: Manual builds need repository access and an approved revision. Take CHAIN_ID, GENESIS_FAUCET_ADDRESS, BOOTSTRAP_ADDRESS, BOOTSTRAP_PEERS and fee parameters from the published v2 network configuration at https://node.peopleblockchain.network/network. Use a separate data directory for a different chain.

items.title: 02 · Prepare the environment
items.text: Use Node.js 22 and npm. In the repository you received, check out the approved SHA and run the commands below. Building is required: packages load dist. CPU, memory and disk requirements still need measurement; there is no universal server size yet.

items.title: 03 · Prepare .env.node
items.text: Set PEER_ID, CHAIN_ID, GENESIS_FAUCET_ADDRESS, BOOTSTRAP_ADDRESS, BOOTSTRAP_PEERS, DATA_DIR, PORT=4001, GOSSIP_PORT=4002 and BIND_HOST=127.0.0.1 in .env.node. EXPECTED_GENESIS_HASH must match genesisHash in the public configuration; TOKEN_CREATE_MIN_FEE and NFT_MINT_MIN_FEE must match its fees. PUBLIC_GOSSIP_URL is only needed for a node accepting inbound gossip connections.

items.title: 04 · Use public settings only
items.text: GENESIS_FAUCET_ADDRESS and BOOTSTRAP_ADDRESS are public addresses. DEV_FAUCET_PRIVATE_KEY stays with the faucet and BOOTSTRAP_PRIVATE_KEY stays with the designated initial-block producer. Do not request or copy these secrets to your node.

items.title: 05 · Start the process
items.text: Save .env.node inside people-node in your Peoples-Blockchain checkout and restrict file permissions. Do not enable ALLOW_FAUCET or ALLOW_DEV_ENDPOINTS on an ordinary node. Do not expose the HTTP API to the internet without agreed protection.

sections.code:
git clone https://github.com/rednaxelavoroge/Peoples-Blockchain.git
cd Peoples-Blockchain/people-node
npm ci
npm run build
node --env-file=.env.node apps/node/dist/index.js

sections.title: Become a validator
sections.lead: Run and synchronize an ordinary node first, then coordinate participation with the operator.

items.title: Separate key and bond
items.text: Create a dedicated validator key and keep it safe. Obtain test PPL for the bond and fee, and confirm current registration parameters and the waiting period. Registration uses a signed join operation; starting a server alone does not register a validator.

items.title: Enable the role
items.text: After registration, configure the matching VALIDATOR_ADDRESS and VALIDATOR_PRIVATE_KEY in the node environment and restart. Follow the operator’s instructions for the approved network version and verify actual participation in blocks.

items.title: Availability matters
items.text: In the approved v2 mode, an unavailable selected validator stops block production. Safe automatic producer rotation is not implemented yet. Coordinate maintenance with the operator; do not reset the chain yourself.

sections.title: Participation Power and rewards
sections.lead: How your share of the Community Pool is counted. Numbers marked as provisional can still change.

items.title: Participation Power
items.text: A personal weight that sets your share of Community Pool payouts from network fees in PPL. You cannot sell or transfer it.

items.title: Limits per person and epochs
items.text: Participation is counted in periods called epochs. Extra activity brings less and less, and each person has a hard limit, so one account cannot take the whole pool.

items.title: Where the pool money comes from
items.text: 25% of eligible network fees go to the Community Pool and are paid out each epoch to active participants who qualify.

items.title: Protection from fake accounts
items.text: New accounts gain weight slowly, inactive ones lose it, and limits stop a group of fake accounts from earning much.

items.title: When nobody qualifies
items.text: If no one qualifies in an epoch, nothing is paid out as free income. The pool keeps the money under the protocol rules.

sections.title: How the network works
sections.lead: The parts of the network and the rules no one can change by hand.

items.title: Consensus and validators
items.text: Dedicated validators create and confirm blocks. Phones and browser tabs take part in the network but are not validators.

items.title: State and storage
items.text: Each node keeps the chain state on its own disk. Ordinary nodes may delete old blocks; validators restart from their own data folder.

items.title: Fixed rules
items.text: Fee shares, supply rules and accounting are written into the protocol code, so a website text cannot change them.

sections.title: What you can use
sections.lead: What already works on the test network and what comes after it. No mainnet date is set.

items.title: Available now · test network
items.text: Wallet, token and NFT factory, swaps for test PPL, contracts and fee routing.

items.title: Available now · human network
items.text: One-tap participation from your phone, a check that you are a real person without biometrics, and participation points for your share of the Community Pool.

items.title: After that · apps for everyone
items.text: The Hub and tools for creators, built on the same protocol.

sections.title: PPL — the network coin
sections.lead: People (PPL) pays for network fees and protocol actions on this chain.

items.title: Test coins
items.text: Test PPL is for trying the network. Holding test PPL does not mean profit.

items.title: Fees only in PPL
items.text: Transfers, creating a token or NFT, and contract gas are all priced in PPL.

sections.title: Keep your wallet safe
sections.lead: Whoever holds the secret can sign operations.

items.title: Your recovery phrase is yours alone
items.text: Never send your phrase, private key or password to support, a chat, a website form or a repository. A public address and transaction ID are enough to investigate an operation.

items.title: Before signing
items.text: Check the domain, network, recipient, amount and purpose. Try a small amount first. A blockchain does not provide the usual cancellation of an accidental transfer.

items.title: If you lose access
items.text: Look for your own backup of the phrase or key. A website password and chain data cannot recover a lost private key. Do not trust offers to “recover” it for a fee.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.lead: What to check when something does not work.

items.title: Network unavailable
items.text: The site cannot reach the network right now. Wait and refresh the page. Do not re-enter secrets into third-party services.

items.title: I sent a transfer but the balance did not change
items.text: Check the transaction ID, block inclusion and network state in the explorer. Check the address and selected network. Do not send a duplicate transfer before finding out what happened to the first.

items.title: New blocks stopped appearing
items.text: Connectivity or an unavailable selected validator may be responsible. Report the observed height and time to the operator. Do not delete node data to try to fix a halt.

items.title: What to include in a support report
items.text: Page address, error text, time, public address and transaction ID. Node operators can add the code SHA, CHAIN_ID and height. Remove secrets from logs; do not send your .env file.

nodeQuickStart.title: Your node — one command
nodeQuickStart.intro: Install and start Docker. The command below runs a verifying follower node with persistent storage on the public testnet. No wallet, bond or private keys are required.
nodeQuickStart.copyManual: Select the command and copy it manually.
nodeQuickStart.hint: Check: curl http://127.0.0.1:4001/health should return ok:true and chainId people-public-testnet-v2-2026-09-30. Logs: docker logs people-node. Stop: docker stop people-node. Start again: docker start people-node. Update image: docker stop people-node && docker rm people-node, then run the command again (keep volume people-node-data).
